run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: I inspected the social-network namespace end to end: workload/pod state, owner chains, events (all namespaces), Services/Endpoints, ConfigMaps, PVC/PV, nodes, NetworkPolicies/ResourceQuotas, Prometheus, Jaeger and Loki. All 26 application microservice/database Deployments are at 1/1 ready with zero restarts, every application Service has endpoints, and the sampled request path is clean: Jaeger shows only HTTP 200 on /wrk2-api/post/compose, /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read and /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read with no error spans (03:59:46–03:59:57), and the wrk2 load pod reported 1024 requests in 10s at 102 req/s with no non-2xx lines. The one concrete failing object state in the namespace is the tracing backend: Deployment jaeger declares 2 replicas with required pod anti-affinity on kubernetes.io/hostname and mounts the ReadWriteOnce claim jaeger-pvc, whose PV is pinned by node affinity to sregym-worker2. Consequently only one jaeger pod runs (on sregym-worker2) and pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-llkmj is Pending with PodScheduled=False/Unschedulable. That is the deepest cause the evidence supports and is reported as root cause, but I could not confirm user-visible request failure: Prometheus has no application metrics for this namespace (no kube-state-metrics series for social-network, no traces_span_metrics_calls_total), Jaeger held only ~12 seconds of traces, and the Redis source was unreachable, so absence of app-level error signals is an observability gap rather than proof of health. Startup MongoDB createIndex failures at 03:59:35–03:59:39 are startup races; the same services answered successfully afterwards.

claims.text: All 26 non-Jaeger Deployments in social-network report ready=1/available=1 for replicas=1, and all 28 pods in the namespace have phase Running with container ready=true and restartCount 0, except the Jaeger pod described below.

Deployment jaeger in namespace social-network declares spec.replicas=2 with required podAntiAffinity topologyKey kubernetes.io/hostname on label service=jaeger, mounts persistentVolumeClaim jaeger-pvc, and its status shows readyReplicas=1, availableReplicas=1 of 2 (last applied by kubectl-client-side-apply at 2026-11-24T03:59:41Z).

Pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-llkmj is Pending with PodScheduled=False, reason Unschedulable, message "0/4 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match pod anti-affinity rules, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 2 node(s) had volume node affinity conflict"; the sibling pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-q8ff6 is Running and Ready on node sregym-worker2.

PersistentVolumeClaim jaeger-pvc (social-network) is Bound, ReadWriteOnce, 1Gi, storageClass openebs-hostpath; its PersistentVolume pvc-8820aa4f-faf6-4967-8941-0fb0288b3cc1 has required nodeAffinity kubernetes.io/hostname In [sregym-worker2], so the volume can only be used by a pod on sregym-worker2.

Two FailedScheduling events were recorded (inside the authorized window) for object jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-llkmj with exactly those scheduling reasons (anti-affinity, control-plane taint, no available persistent volume / volume node affinity conflict).
A cluster-wide pod scan found exactly one non-Running pod (jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-llkmj, Pending) and zero Running pods with a not-ready container; the second list was empty.

In the sampled traces (03:59:46.866Z–03:59:57.733Z) all nginx-web-server spans for /wrk2-api/post/compose, /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read and /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read carry http.status_code=200, span_groups shows error_rows=0 for every (service, operation) group, and durations are small (compose_post_server 7284–7509 µs, read_home_timeline_server 327–888 µs, read_user_timeline_server 1401–1720 µs).

The wrk2 load pod wrk2-job-wpd5m reported for round #0 against http://10.96.23.170:8080/wrk2-api/post/compose: "1024 requests in 10.00s", "Requests/sec: 102.38", with no non-2xx/socket-error lines, and started round #1 at 03:59:53Z.

Every application Service (compose-post-service, home-timeline-service, media-frontend, media-service, nginx-thrift, post-storage-service, social-graph-service, text-service, unique-id-service, url-shorten-service, user-service, user-mention-service, user-timeline-service and their redis/mongodb/memcached Services) has a populated Endpoints subset; the only Services without endpoints are jaeger, jaeger-agent, jaeger-collector and jaeger-query, which also declare no ports.

No NetworkPolicy and no ResourceQuota objects exist anywhere in the cluster (both queries processed 0 items), all 4 nodes are Ready, and only sregym-control-plane carries the node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane NoSchedule taint.

All 27 Deployments in social-network (including jaeger) were created within 2026-11-24T03:59:34Z–03:59:41Z, are at metadata.generation 1 with deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 1, and were applied by manager helm except jaeger, which was applied by manager kubectl-client-side-apply at 03:59:41Z — i.e. no rolling update of an existing workload occurred in the window.

At pod start-up (03:59:35Z–03:59:39Z) user-service, url-shorten-service and social-graph-service logged "Failed to create mongodb index, try again" / "Error in createIndexes: No suitable servers found: serverSelectionTimeoutMS expired ... 'user-mongodb:27017'" (same pattern for url-shorten-mongodb and social-graph-mongodb).

Those start-up MongoDB failures did not persist into failure: in the same window the same services produced successful spans (social-graph-service get_followers_server 869–1010 µs, url-shorten-service compose_urls_server 874–961 µs, user-service compose_creator_server 6–8 µs at ~03:59:55Z), and the wrk2 client completed 1024 compose requests in 10s without reporting any non-2xx response.

social-graph-service emits a sustained stream of "<warning>: (SocialGraphHandler.h:612:GetFollowers) user_id: N not found" lines — e.g. 50 lines between 03:59:53.717Z and 03:59:57.904Z and a 20-second count rising 138→167 lines on that pod — while still returning get_followers_server spans without error status.

Prometheus in this target carries no application or trace metrics for the social-network namespace: kube_pod_info by namespace returns only kube-system, openebs, observe, local-path-storage and sregym, kube_deployment_status_replicas_available has no social-network deployment series, and the metric-name inventory contains no traces_span_metrics_calls_total and no service_name label.

Root cause of the pending replica: Deployment jaeger itself renders the second replica unschedulable — it asks for 2 replicas while requiring hostname-level anti-affinity between them and giving both the same ReadWriteOnce PVC whose PV is pinned to sregym-worker2 by node affinity, so with the control-plane taint no node satisfies all three constraints; the tracing backend therefore runs single-replica with reduced redundancy rather than the two replicas the Deployment asks for.

The GetFollowers "user_id not found" warnings most likely reflect an empty follow graph in the freshly created social-graph database (no follow edges yet for the random user ids used by the load generator), which would make home-timeline reads return empty results; this is not confirmed as a fault — the RPCs return without error status and HTTP status is 200, so whether this is intended fresh-state behaviour or a data-population problem is unresolved.

Rejected: a media-frontend port mismatch as a fault. Deployment media-frontend declares containerPort 8081 while Service media-frontend maps port 8081 to targetPort 8080, but the media-frontend ConfigMap nginx.conf contains "listen 8080 reuseport", so the Service maps to the correct listening port and the declared containerPort is informational only.

Set Deployment jaeger/spec.replicas to 1, or if two replicas are required, give each replica its own dynamically provisioned claim (or a RWX/object-store backed Jaeger store) and relax the requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution hostname anti-affinity to preferred, so a second replica can be scheduled.

Have kube-state-metrics (and an application/trace metric pipeline exposing service_name based series such as traces_span_metrics_calls_total) scrape the social-network namespace so app-level error rate and latency can be evaluated instead of inferred from short trace samples.

gaps: No application-level metrics exist for social-network in this Prometheus (no kube-state-metrics series for the namespace, no traces_span_metrics_calls_total, no service_name label), so error-rate and latency series for the microservices are unknown, not zero; no error-rate baseline exists.

Jaeger held only traces from 03:59:46Z to 03:59:57Z (the jaeger pod started 03:59:45Z and keeps only recent traces in memory), and with a 1% probabilistic sampler plus a 5-trace/10-trace sample only three nginx operations and one compose request flow were examined; requests outside the sample are unknown.

The whole social-network application was created at 03:59:34Z–03:59:46Z, only ~24 seconds before the authorized window end, so no pre-incident healthy baseline exists for any latency or availability comparison.

The Redis data source was unreachable (redis_info returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so redis health/keyspace of home-timeline-redis, social-graph-redis, user-timeline-redis and compose-post-redis could not be checked.

The change_history integration is not available, so who/why created Deployment jaeger with replicas=2 at 03:59:41Z cannot be verified beyond the kubectl-client-side-apply last-write timestamp (not a full change history).

wrk2 round #1 started at 03:59:53Z and its results fall after the authorized window end, and the wrk2 Job object no longer exists (jobs list is empty), so the outcome of the register/follow/read workloads could not be observed.

Queries for application-log errors after 03:59:40Z (excluding the createIndex noise) and for nginx-thrift logs in 03:40–03:59Z returned no_data, so "no persistent application error" rests on the sampled spans and wrk2 output, not on a complete log scan.

The meaning of the social-graph-service "GetFollowers user_id: N not found" warnings (empty follow graph vs. a data-population defect) could not be verified because there is no MongoDB read access and no application metrics.
Whether the reduced Jaeger replica count caused any trace loss or tracing outage could not be verified; the redcued capacity is only observed as a scheduling failure of one replica.
next_steps: Check who or what created Deployment jaeger with replicas=2 and a RWO PVC at 2026-11-24T03:59:41Z (audit log / GitOps source), and whether that is the intended topology.
Add a stable, longer-lived tracing store/higher sampling or an application metrics exporter for social-network so the request path can be evaluated over minutes rather than a ~12 second trace buffer.

Verify data population of the social graph (follow edges) and compare home-timeline read results against the expected seeded state to decide whether the GetFollowers "not found" warnings are benign fresh-state behaviour.

Re-run the wrk2 workload rounds beyond the current window and watch per-endpoint non-2xx counts and latency percentiles for /wrk2-api/post/compose, /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read and /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read.
Enable kube-state-metrics for the social-network namespace and confirm app pods' restart/ready series appear in Prometheus.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
